relations.myth: Atum grants Geb his heritage and the Ennead
relations.note: Atum invests Geb with divine inheritance and authority over the Ennead.
Geb is explicitly called Shu’s eldest son.
Shu separates Geb from Nut by raising her above the earth.

relations.myth: Geb usurps Shu and commits a dynastic offense
relations.note: Late texts accuse Geb of displacing or offending Shu through Tefnut.
Tefnut is Geb’s mother in the Heliopolitan genealogy.

relations.myth: Geb lies with his mother after displacing Shu
relations.note: Late disputed traditions describe a sexual offense, possibly coercive, involving Geb and Tefnut.
Nut is Geb’s sister in the Heliopolitan divine genealogy.
Geb and Nut are sexual partners and parents of the Osirian generation.
Osiris is a son of Geb and Nut.

relations.myth: Geb heals and protects the dead Osiris
relations.note: Mortuary texts ask Geb to heal, protect, and sustain his son Osiris.
Divine kingship and legitimate sovereignty pass from Geb to Osiris.
relations.source: Pyramid Texts and Turin Royal Canon

relations.note: Isis is a daughter of Geb and Nut.
Seth is a son of Geb and Nut.

relations.myth: Geb adjudicates Seth’s claim against Horus
relations.note: Geb initially assigns Seth part of Egypt, then awards unified rule to Horus.

relations.myth: Geb assigns Upper Egypt to Seth
relations.note: In an initial territorial settlement, Geb gives Seth one portion of Egypt.
Nephthys is a daughter of Geb and Nut.
Geb is Horus’s grandfather through Osiris.

relations.myth: Geb adjudicates Horus’s claim against Seth
relations.note: Geb recognizes Horus as Osiris’s rightful heir over Seth.

relations.myth: Geb grants Horus the united land
relations.note: Geb awards Horus the whole of Egypt and confirms his inherited throne.

relations.myth: Arueris is born on an intercalary day
relations.note: Plutarch includes Arueris among the five children of Geb and Nut.

relations.myth: Ra charges Geb with terrestrial snakes
relations.note: Ra consults or commissions Geb concerning snakes arising from the earth.

relations.myth: Ptah creates the gods through heart and tongue
relations.note: Memphite theology places Geb and the Ennead within Ptah’s creative activity.
Some mortuary traditions make the serpent Nehebkau a son of Geb.
Some later genealogical syntheses pair Geb and Renenutet as Nehebkau’s parents.
Greco-Roman interpretation equates Geb with the old divine king Kronos.

relations.myth: Divine judgment of Horus and Seth
relations.note: Thoth articulates verdicts while Geb supplies ancestral territorial authority.
Geb stands at the Ennead’s head as judge with authoritative speech.

relations.myth: Geb nourishes and vivifies the Ennead
relations.note: As ka of the gods, Geb brings, nourishes, and causes them to live.
